The upgrade comes after Iranian missile strikes exposed vulnerabilities in Israel's air defense network and placed increasing pressure on its stockpiles of interceptors.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s government prefers a joint operation with the US “in the short term,” but it remains unclear whether President Trump is prepared to authorize further strikes on Iran, CBS News reports.
Israel’s military is ready for another round of fighting and remains on high alert, as US forces in the Middle East include tens of thousands of personnel, two aircraft carriers and their strike groups.
👉 A possible new US offensive could be launched within two to four days if Trump gives the order, given the American military assets already deployed in the region amid an exchange of strikes between Iran and the US, including an attack on Iran’s strategic Qeshm Island earlier this week.
The US president previously sent mixed signals, threatening to use force against Iran while also saying that he is not rushing into a decision and that the standoff could continue into 2027.
Months of the Iran-US indirect talks have failed to produce a deal on reopening the Strait of Hormuz. Tehran has refused to discuss its nuclear program unless Washington lifts its naval blockade and accepts six other conditions, including an end to hostilities on all fronts in the Middle East. 
Iran also warned that any renewed attack would trigger a broader response, threatening to target Israel and US military installations across the Gulf and Europe, as well as energy infrastructure and undersea internet cables.
